part_title: Step Functions, ML Orchestration and Resilience

scenes.title: AWS Step Functions
scenes.narration: AWS Step Functions coordinates a workflow as a state machine with explicit transitions, inputs and results. States can invoke AWS services, make choices, wait, run parallel branches and catch failures. This makes it useful when an AI application needs more than a single Lambda execution, for example document extraction followed by quality checks and model enrichment. Standard and Express workflows have different durability, execution and pricing characteristics, so choose based on duration, volume and delivery requirements. Retry policies should account for throttling and transient failures without hiding persistent errors. The workflow definition captures orchestration; each task integration still needs correct IAM permissions and appropriately sized payloads. A Step Functions execution records transitions so operators can identify exactly which task failed and what error path was taken, rather than searching one large function's logs.

scenes.title: Step Functions Example: Training a Machine Learning Model
scenes.narration: A model-training workflow can begin by validating data locations and configuration, then start a SageMaker training job through a service integration. The state machine waits for an outcome, checks whether the job succeeded and routes either to evaluation or to a failure-handling branch. Evaluation metrics should be compared with explicit thresholds before a model is registered or approved for deployment. Decouple the orchestration from the actual compute: Step Functions tracks state and transitions, while SageMaker performs training. Build in timeouts, retries for transient API errors and clear failure reporting. Capture dataset and model artifact identifiers so experiments can be reproduced and audited. If training succeeds but evaluation fails, route to a rejected-model state instead of registering the artifact for production. Training completion and approval are separate gates.

scenes.title: Step Functions Example: Tuning a Machine Learning Model
scenes.narration: Hyperparameter tuning runs multiple candidate training configurations and compares their performance. Step Functions can launch a SageMaker tuning job, track completion and then retrieve the preferred candidate for evaluation. The search strategy and objective metric must be set carefully; optimizing one validation metric does not guarantee the model behaves acceptably in production. Limit cost with sensible training budgets, parallelism and early stopping where supported. Handle job failure, quota exhaustion and cancellation through well-defined state transitions. The state machine should pass artifact references and metrics rather than large datasets. This pattern shows why workflow orchestration is preferable to forcing an extended tuning operation into one Lambda invocation. Watch the objective metric and job budget together. The best reported candidate is still only a candidate until it passes a separate evaluation dataset.

scenes.title: Step Functions Example: Managing a Batch Job
scenes.narration: A batch workflow starts a managed processing task, waits for its completion and branches based on success or failure. It might ingest S3 data, run a transformation job, validate output and publish the resulting location for downstream consumers. Step Functions can coordinate services such as AWS Batch or SageMaker processing without performing the heavy computation itself. Use a job identifier to correlate state transitions with processing logs. Avoid huge state payloads by passing S3 URIs and metadata. Design an error path for retries, failed inputs and partial output. In a GenAI pipeline, batch jobs may create embeddings or enrich documents before a search index is refreshed. For failed batch jobs, store the job ID and output prefix; a rerun should not silently mix partial outputs from the old and new attempts.

scenes.title: AWS Step Functions: State Machines and States
scenes.narration: A state machine is a declarative definition of a workflow, including its states, transitions and error behavior. Task states invoke work, Choice states route based on data, Parallel and Map states manage fan-out, Wait states delay progress, and Succeed or Fail states terminate execution. InputPath, Parameters or Arguments, ResultPath, OutputPath and JSONata-based transformations affect which data moves between states, depending on the query-language configuration. Be deliberate about payload contracts and execution history. Understand where errors are retried versus caught, because retries can repeat side effects. A machine-readable workflow definition improves auditability, but services inside the workflow still need idempotent operations. A Choice state routes based on conditions; a Map processes a collection; a Parallel state runs independent branches. Match each state to a requirement rather than memorising names alone.

scenes.title: Step Functions Circuit Breakers
scenes.narration: A circuit-breaker pattern prevents a failing downstream service from being overwhelmed by repeated requests. In a Step Functions workflow, use retries with bounded exponential backoff for transient errors, then transition to a fallback or controlled failure path when the attempt budget is exhausted. You may also track an external service-health flag before invoking new tasks. Distinguish retryable throttling from validation errors that should fail immediately. An explicit Catch path can send diagnostics, mark an execution for review or route to manual intervention. This is not an automatic built-in circuit-breaker switch for every state; it is a resilience pattern you construct from state transitions and external health signals. A validation error that will never succeed should move directly to a controlled failure path. Repeating it with exponential backoff only wastes time and money.

scenes.title: Step Functions and Generative AI
scenes.narration: Step Functions can coordinate a multi-stage generative AI pipeline: ingest a source, extract relevant content, retrieve context, invoke Bedrock, validate output and notify a downstream consumer. Each stage has different latency, data-size and permission needs. A state machine makes those transitions, retries and audit events visible. For batch processing, consider a Map state with bounded concurrency rather than launching every model request simultaneously and exhausting quotas. Put human review or approval at critical business decisions where required. Avoid putting private source documents or large prompt bodies directly into the workflow execution history; pass restricted S3 references and only necessary metadata. For a document summarisation workflow, the state machine can track extraction, retrieval, model invocation and approval while each worker stores substantial output in S3.

scenes.title: Step Functions: Payload Size and Data Passing
scenes.narration: Step Functions passes JSON state between workflow steps, but there are payload-size and history limits. Large documents, images or model artifacts should be stored in S3, and workflow states should pass an object URI, version identifier and minimal metadata. Use input and output transformations to prevent accidental growth as each task appends results. Some integrations can use distributed processing or supported item readers for larger datasets. Persist secrets outside execution payloads, and consider what administrators can see in logs and execution history. The objective is to orchestrate work reliably while keeping state compact, secure and easy to debug. This principle is especially important for multimodal GenAI pipelines. The source document should remain in S3; a compact state might contain only its bucket, object key and processing status. Remove verbose model responses before passing to the next state.
